newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end sharply up in end-of-month buying.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end sharply up in end-of-month buying.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed sharply higher on Friday as investors went on a month's end buying spree, with heavy speculation in benchmark Telebras ahead of mid-February options settlements, brokers said.
"It's the end of January, so players were closing out books," said John Carioba of Indusval brokerage. "Also, we're getting close to options expiration."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares surged 2.26 percent to 79,647 points in strong turnover of 540.2 million reais ($517 milliion).
Telebras shares and options accounted for a majority of the day's turnover.

The rise among leading blue chips was led by state oil firm Petrobras as investors continued to snap up the share on the upbeat outlook for the firm and promising news about Brazil's planned new Oil Law, brokers said.
Petrobras preferred rose 4.69 percent to end at 201 reais and its voting common ended 4.26 percent higher at 159 reais.
Among other leaders, state-owned power holding Eletrobras closed up 2.4 percent at 427 reais.
Eletrobras led the rise in the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid shares, which rose 1.72 percent to close at 2,292 points.
Meanwhile, state mining firm Cia Vale do Rio Doce's (CVRD) blue-chip preferred share closed up 2.61 percent to end at 23.60 while its voting common ended off 0.36 percent at 27.80 reais.
